source_law.text: When the signal is circular green alone: Pedestrians facing such a signal may proceed across the highway within any marked or unmarked crosswalk, unless directed otherwise by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

legal_analysis_note: The 307(2)(b) circular-green crosswalk clause grants permission unless another device directs otherwise under 484B.283. It does not itself define a pedestrian violation. A governing pedestrian indication must be source-observed at entry and during the crossing; the authored request is not evidence that the head physically faces or governs the pedestrian. The 484B.283(1)(d) alternatives distinguish Walk, flashing Dont Walk with countdown, flashing Dont Walk without countdown, and steady Dont Walk; their timing and continuation clauses are separate legal questions. These four selected cases contrast Walk and steady Dont Walk at entry under circular green and do not assert complete 484B.283 coverage or legal outcome. Physical pixel/governance review and original Native readback remain required.
